title: Lyapunov-controlled thermalization: an exact real-time example
abstract: A verified Kubo-Martin-Schwinger (KMS) relation, after a drive has ceased, is not sufficient evidence to prove equilibrium. We demonstrate this in a large-$N$ large-$q$ Sachdev-Ye-Kitaev (SYK) quench protocol. Although all post-quench fermion correlators are exactly thermal, a second quench back to the initial Hamiltonian reveals hidden memory of the initial state. It is encoded in correlators connecting to times before the first quench. This memory is an extensive nonequilibrium (NEQ) witness with its decay rate being the Lyapunov exponent $λ_L$. Thus $λ_L$ sets the rate at which the state becomes effectively indistinguishable from a Gibbs state. Despite being a unitary interacting many-body system, the complete NEQ real-time evolution is obtained exactly in the large-$N$, large-$q$ limit, making the setup ideal for analytically studying thermalization.
summary: This paper investigates the true nature of thermalization in the SYK model by analyzing a 'double quench' protocol. It proves that merely satisfying the KMS condition is insufficient for equilibrium, as a measurable, non-equilibrium memory persists. This memory decays exponentially at a rate $\lambda_L$, which characterizes the rate at which the system approaches a true Gibbs state.
main_problem: To rigorously determine the conditions under which a unitary quantum system achieves true thermal equilibrium, demonstrating that satisfying a Kubo-Martin-Schwinger (KMS) relation is insufficient evidence.
main_result: The system retains a measurable, non-equilibrium memory of its initial state, which decays exponentially at a rate identified as the Lyapunov exponent, $\lambda_L$.
method: The authors employ a 'double quench' protocol on the Sachdev-Ye-Kitaev (SYK) model, solving the Kadanoff-Baym equation (KBE) in the large-$N$ limit to track non-equilibrium observables.
model_or_system: The study uses the large-$N$ large-$q$ Sachdev-Ye-Kitaev (SYK) model, a strongly interacting system, subjected to piecewise-constant coupling quenches. The analysis focuses on the real-time evolution of two-point correlation functions.

important_parameters: Large-$N$ limit, large-$q$ limit, waiting time $\delta t$, and the Lyapunov exponent $\lambda_L$.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the large-$N$ limit and the solvability of the KBE via block-wise recursion across quench intervals.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the schematic of the return-quench protocol and the partitioning of the time-correlation plane into blocks used for the recursive solution of the KBE.
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the problem by showing that post-quench correlators satisfying KMS are insufficient. It then develops the mathematical machinery by solving the KBE block-by-block for the SYK model. Finally, it analyzes the return-quench protocol to extract the memory witness, finding its decay rate $\lambda_L$.
why_interesting: The work provides a concrete, analytically solvable model (SYK) to study non-equilibrium dynamics, directly addressing the fundamental question of thermalization rates ($\lambda_L$) in a manner relevant to holographic theories.
